action_items.task: Look into the programming of how menus are shown on TVs and how they are programmed.
Play with play-dough and work on the look and feel of the design and user interface design.

decisions.text: The remote control will not include a built-in screen.
Two prototypes will be created to test user preference.
Batteries will be used as the power source.

notes:
## Component Design and Materials
- Custom design needed for case (hard plastic or other material) and circuit board; standard parts include buttons, wheels, infrared LED, radio sender/receiver, and beeper.
- Material options include rubber, plastic, wood, or titanium; titanium is rejected due to weight and flat-case limitation, and rubber requires rubber buttons.
- iPod-style wheel requires a more expensive 'regular' grade chip instead of the minimal chip.
- Marketing Expert expressed a dislike for spongy materials but agreed a stress ball-like texture could provide a nice feel.
- User Interface Designer suggested integrating the fruit/vegetable theme into the tactile feel, perhaps making the whole device feel like a stress ball.
- Marketing Expert proposed using covers to change the device's appearance, similar to mobile phone cases, rather than creating specific fruit-shaped objects.
## Screen vs. Wheel Interface
- User Interface Designer suggested a screen on the TV to handle menus and channel selection for large channel lists, while the remote would only have a wheel.
- Industrial Designer noted that adding a screen requires an advanced chip, making it more expensive than the minimal or regular chip options.
- Project Manager considered that a screen would be better for managing many options, but User Interface Designer agreed it might be silly if rarely used.
## Remote Form Factor and Controls
- User Interface Designer proposed a small, circular handheld device controlled by a wheel, similar to a wheely remote control.
- Project Manager asked if the device would need buttons besides power, and User Interface Designer suggested the menu button could be held longer to turn on the TV.
- Project Manager suggested adding a coverable panel for less-used functions like contrast adjustment to keep the design clean.
## Shape and Design
- The squishy part should be detachable so users can swap different fruit and vegetable shapes.
- The squishy part will mould to the user's hand automatically.
- The fruit and vegetable colours will match either the plastic face on the front or the squishy part underneath.
- The company colour is silver and yellow.
- The logo needs to be placed somewhere on the device.
- The batteries must fit under the plastic case.
- The squishy part and the rest of the device should be a single unit that can snap off.
## Power Source
- Options discussed included batteries, solar power, a dynamo (bicycle mechanism), and a kinetic wind-up mechanism.
- Solar power was considered but deemed weird for a living room setting.
- The dynamo creates energy automatically when moved, which is seen as cool.
## Prototyping
- Two prototypes will be created to test which design users prefer.
tldr: The team finalized the design of a fruit/vegetable themed TV remote with a detachable squishy part, decided on batteries as the power source, and agreed to create two prototypes for user testing.
